items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest and the General Nature Thereof
notes: Councillor Freeman declared a pecuniary interest with respect to a closed meeting due to a conflict of interest as it relates to their place of employment.

items.title: Closed Meeting
notes: Council meeting recessed: (Time: 2:04 p.m.)
Council meeting reconvened: (Time: 3:31 p.m.)

items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Mayor McCabe opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.
Mayor McCabe offered further reflections on the reconciliation process.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Mayor McCabe provided Council with a moment of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest and the General Nature Thereof
notes: No disclosure of pecuniary interest was declared by any member of Council at this point in the meeting.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
notes: That the previous meeting minutes be approved.

items.title: Consent Motion
notes: Councillor Vasic requested that item 7a) Waterloo City Centre – Lease Renewal – Uptown BIA be removed from the consent motion.

items.title: Items Removed From the Consent Motion
Waterloo City Centre – Lease Renewal –
notes: Uptown BIA
Report No.: COM2024-046
Prepared By: Liz Williams
Kevin Van Ooteghem responded to questions of Council.

items.title: HAF Community Planning Permit
notes: System Initiative: Draft Community
Planning Permit By-law and Complementary
Urban Design Guidelines
Report No.: IPPW2024-057
Prepared By: Tanja Curic
Tanja Curic offered introductory remarks on the report and introduced the consultants.

David Riley, Principal, SGL Planning & Design Inc. gave a presentation outlining the Community Planning Permit System, including the differences and similarities between the traditional processes and the proposed processes. He then responded to questions of Council. Tanja Curic also responded to questions of Council. Catherine Jay, Principal, SGL Planning & Design Inc. and Justine Giancola, Partner, Dillon Consulting Limited also responded to questions of Council.

items.title: 2024 Get READI Plan
notes: Report No.: CAO2024-029
Prepared By: Divya Handa

Divya Handa gave a presentation outlining the Get READI Plan, including the changes made since the draft plan was presented in September 2024, as well as the key themes and findings. She then responded to questions of Council. Amy Ross also responded to questions of Council.

Sarah Shafiq, Director of Advocacy, Research and Outreach, Coalition of Muslim Women of KW spoke about the journey that the Coalition of Muslim Women (CMW) has taken since beginning 14 years ago, as well as the work CMW is doing now to address hate in the Region and across Canada. She then responded to questions of Council.
Jim Bowman also responded to questions of Council.
In response to the delegation request, Council considered the following motion:

items.title: Public Meetings
notes: Formal Public Meeting

items.title: Zoning By-law Amendment Z-24-14,
notes: Station Area Mixed-Use (SAMU) Zone,
The Corporation of the City of Waterloo
Report No.: IPPW2024-044
Prepared By: Tristin Deveau
Ward No.: Wards 3 (Lakeshore), 4 (Northeast), and
6 (Central-Columbia)
Tristin Deveau gave a presentation outlining the proposed zoning amendment, including the link to the Housing Accelerator Fund, and the specific guidelines for the new zone.
He then responded to questions of Council.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Formal Public Meeting and advised the application is now open to Council for a motion and debate.

items.title: Questions
notes: Councillor Vasic had a couple questions of staff regarding the “Safer Municipalities Act” tabled by the Province, and asked what the City’s current approach to encampments is and how the City offers support. Nicole Papke provided an overview of the process and cooperation with the Region of Waterloo. In response to questions regarding the legislation, staff indicated they are monitoring if there is a City of Waterloo impact.
Councillor Vasic asked if a briefing note could be prepared in the New Year with a preliminary review of the legislation.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Vasic wanted to thank the Cardinal Crescent neighbours who did Christmas on Cardinal Crescent, with a lights competition and hot chocolate.

Mayor McCabe mentioned that tonight in Alexandra Park there is a Christmas Carol sing-along. She extended warm wishes to the community, whatever people are celebrating over the Season of Many Holidays.

items.title: Adjournment
notes: READ AND APPROVED, January 20, 2025
Mayor
City Clerk
